evidence_quotes.name_asked_and_used: Joanna asks 'This is Jana' and then uses 'Jana' or 'Gina' (pronunciation variation) multiple times: 'no worries and I guess here that you're planning', 'So typically for a house, the size again this might still change Jana'
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna says 'it might take about ten to fifteen minutes' and mentions the call purpose, but does NOT explicitly frame the dependable quote promise or wait for a yes before continuing—she moves directly into open-ended concern check
evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Joanna asks 'aside from the pricing, do you have any important concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' before any probing, though this is a slight variation from the standard two-concerns script about movers showing up on time or damage
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer answered 'No, I don't think so' to the concerns question, so no layers were needed—N/A applies
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Customer raised no concerns, so no reflection was needed—N/A applies
evidence_quotes.promises_delivered: Joanna mentions 'no worries damage coverage' ($2,000 coverage for accidental damages, already included) and 'on time guarantee' (discounts if run late) during the pricing explanation in step 5, but these are delivered AFTER probing has already begun and without a permission lead-in asking 'can I share how we work.' They are also delivered as part of the pricing framing rather than as standalone promises addressing the customer's initial concerns
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Joanna does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent after delivering the promises
evidence_quotes.concern_led_opening: Joanna does not explicitly ask 'What items in this move are you most concerned about?' but she does ask 'Are you as any, any other items that you think is oversized like a piano workout equipment, a safe maybe' which is concern-adjacent. She then gathers extensive logistics: two-story homes, 4 bedrooms + office, game room, garage, patio, grill, appliances (refrigerator, washer, dryer with electric confirmation), fragile items, parking at both locations, new home room count (media room), driving distance justification for walkthrough
evidence_quotes.packing_and_box_count: Joanna asks both: 'Are you planning to do the packing yourself or do you need help with packing as well?' (answer: self-packing) and 'typically for a house this size, we usually end up with about $140 to $180 boxes in total' with follow-up about staying in range
evidence_quotes.value_days: Joanna mentions that Friday and Saturday are regular rates at $111/hour, while 'Sundays to Thursdays are more, I mean our best value days it has lower hourly rates' and asks 'just let us know whichever works better especially if you're really preferred date is on the Saturday.' However, the customer is on Saturday the 24th (not a Best Value Day), so this is a legitimate offer. The saving is NOT given as a total dollar figure—only hourly rates are compared ($111/hour regular vs. unspecified lower rate on best value days). This is partial, not full
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Not applicable—this call routes to virtual walkthrough. No explicit ask for the business is made. Joanna says 'I'll just send you like a general pricing again for, for the more personalized estimate we'll be able to give that once we conduct your virtual walkthrough' and closes with 'I'll send that link to you for Friday...just let us know if there'll be any questions or changes ahead of time.' No rate lock mentioned, no explicit booking ask on this call

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details methodically across rooms, appliances, fragile items, and both locations, then seamlessly routed the customer to a virtual walkthrough with a specific time (Friday 1:00 PM) rather than leaving it open-ended.
coaching_note: Move the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) into step 3 with a permission lead-in before probing begins, and deliver them as direct answers to the customer's initial concerns rather than as features buried in the pricing explanation.
